name: congenital heart disease overview
title: Congenital heart disease decision chart: pink or blue, then pulmonary blood flow, sorts the lesions into left-to-right shunts (atrial and ventricular septal defects, patent ductus), obstruction (coarctation), right-to-left shunts (tetralogy of Fallot), separate circulations (transposition) and mixing lesions (truncus, TAPVR), each with its presentation, exam and treatment

root.title: Suspected congenital heart disease (CHD): is the child PINK or BLUE? Then how much PULMONARY BLOOD FLOW (PBF)?
lines: infant in heart failure: poor feeding, sweating with feeds, failure to thrive, tachypnea, big liver
ECG + chest X-ray: lung markings show the flow  →  ECHO is usually definitive

groups.title: BLUE: is it the HEART? Hyperoxia test
lines: PaO2 stays < 100–150 on 100% oxygen → cardiac (lungs: rises to ~600)
every cyanotic lesion needs SURGERY to survive

tiers.title: ↑ PBF: LEFT-TO-RIGHT shunt
lines: the SIZE of the hole decides the symptoms

tiers.title: ↓ PBF: RIGHT-TO-LEFT
lines: also tricuspid atresia: staged single-ventricle palliation

head: h
Atrial septal defect (ASD)
often first found in ADULTS
clue: adults: arrhythmia, pulmonary hypertension, heart failure
• soft ejection murmur, left upper sternal border

head: h
Ventricular septal defect (VSD)
atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) in Down syndrome: septal holes + an abnormal valve
clue: • small: normal S2, no heart failure
• large: SINGLE S2, almost always heart failure
tx: protects the lungs from high pressure

head: h
Coarctation of the aorta
narrowing where the ductus inserts
clue: less flow to the lower body

head: h
Tetralogy of Fallot (ToF)
most common cyanotic CHD overall
right ventricular (RV) outflow block + VSD + overriding aorta + RV hypertrophy
clue: Cyanosis tracks the RV OUTFLOW block
• mild: harsh ejection murmur, late cyanosis
tx: more pulmonary flow when PBF is low
close the VSD, open the RV outflow

head: h
Transposition of the great arteries (TGA)
most common cyanotic CHD in a NEWBORN
clue: • little respiratory distress for the saturation
they let red blood reach the body

head: h
Mixing lesions
truncus arteriosus, and total anomalous pulmonary venous return (TAPVR)
clue: Truncus: ONE artery leaves the heart
TAPVR: lung veins drain to the right
• unobstructed: like a big ASD, mild cyanosis
• OBSTRUCTED: deep cyanosis, lung edema, small heart
